newsitem.title: USA: U.S Northeast spot power firms ahead of cold front.
newsitem.headline: U.S Northeast spot power firms ahead of cold front.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. firmed Wednesday versus Tuesday's levels ahead of the arrival of a weather front that put much of the Midwest in a deep freeze.
The region's temperatures Thursday would run four Fahrenheit degrees below normal in the 20s-40s range, and could fall six to 12 degrees below normal by Friday.
"By Friday, trades will be in the low $30s," said a New York trader.
Extended outlook showed weather would begin to moderate toward seasonal norms Sunday.
Parts of upstate New York could receive heavy snowfall in the next couple of days, while the rest of the Northeast would experience one to two inches of rain.

In western half of the New York Power Pool (NYPP), Thursday electricity for peak, non-firm delivery rose in line with sharply higher spot prices down in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect district.
Peak, non-firm power in western NYPP was talked in the $27.00-$30.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) range, up from Tuesday's $23.00-$24.00.
Western NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Thursday held at $15.00-$16.00.
In eastern NYPP, Thursday power for peak, non-firm delivery was valued higher at $30.00-$31.00, up from Tuesday's assessment of $29.00-$30.00.
Eastern NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Thursday stayed in the $19.00-$20.00 range.
The 832 megawatt (MW) James A Fitzpatrick nuclear plant in Scriba, N.Y., began startup early today after it was manually shut Sunday to repair of a leak in the electrical hydraulic control system.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border was quoted in a $33.00-$35.00/MWh range, compared with Tuesday's quote at $34.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Thursday delivery to the NU border climbed a dollar from Tuesday to the $21.00-$22.00 area.
The 910 MW Maine Yankee nuclear power plant could remain shut until the end of year because it discovered additional problem in an electrical cable system.
The plant was shut December 6 after engineers found a couple of cables to the plant's main control room had been improperly routed.
